previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure (EF 35%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for palpitations and shortness of breath after stopping his heart medications due to financial constraints. He reported sleeping upright due to breathing difficulty, and initial evaluation revealed mild pulmonary edema and elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. ICD interrogation showed NSVT but no shock delivery. Symptoms improved with re-initiation of metoprolol and diuresis using torsemide, later transitioned to furosemide for cost reasons. His condition stabilized with improved respiratory status and weight reduction. Social work assisted with a temporary medication supply, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue all cardiac medications, and follow up for sleep apnea evaluation due to reported snoring.

Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health

right atrium and right ventricle, respectively, appears unchanged.  The heart
is mildly enlarged.  The mediastinal and hilar contours appear unchanged. 
There is a very similar pattern of mild interstitial pulmonary vascular
congestion without significant change.  Fissures appear mildly thickened. 
Very small persistent pleural effusions are suspected, similar to perhaps
slightly decreased.

congestion, with no findings suggestive of superimposed pneumonia.
